public_rationale: CoreWeave's disclosed loan margin is consistent with expensive borrowing for a speculative borrower. JLL also reports substantially cheaper financing for strong-credit tenants. These earlier observations do not settle whether AI data center debt generally was extremely expensive in September. The necessary market coverage and comparable benchmarks remain missing.
limitations: Individual borrowing costs cannot establish the sector-wide claim.
A loan margin is not an all-in yield.
October repricing cannot establish September conditions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data center debt is now extremely expensive.

statement.excerpt: AI data center debt is now extremely expensive.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that borrowing costs are unusually high across AI data center financing, rather than merely high for one distressed borrower.
Compare borrowing rates and spreads with historical levels and comparable infrastructure financing, accounting for maturity, collateral and credit quality.
Use September 1–29, 2026 as the current market observation window. This is an evaluator-selected window because the claim supplies no reporting period.
The surrounding discussion uses market quotations and estimated refinancing costs, so the financial basis is estimate.
criteria.support_condition: Representative September evidence shows unusually high borrowing costs across the relevant financing market, supported by historical or comparable-financing benchmarks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative September evidence shows ordinary or relatively inexpensive borrowing costs across that market after accounting for financing structure and borrower risk.

evidence.explanation: This establishes a substantial contractual margin on one infrastructure-backed facility. It does not establish September all-in borrowing costs or the sector-wide comparison.

evidence.excerpt: Top-tier credit hyperscalers are still yielding the most efficient pricing (low-200 bps credit spreads) and leverage levels up to 85% loan-to-cost.
evidence.locator: Data center financing liquidity remains strong across credit tiers
evidence.explanation: JLL reports materially different pricing for strong-credit tenants, cautioning against generalizing from speculative borrowers. Its August assessment covers broader data center financing rather than a matched September AI-only sample.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative September pricing dataset covering the relevant financing structures, with historical and comparable infrastructure benchmarks and a transparent explanation of what counts as unusually expensive.
